rationale:
Evidence: still no race telemetry, so every expected value is a guess to be tested by the race. I kept the sensor span and reduced kd further, based on the critique's arithmetic check.

Accepted from the round-2 critique:
- Derivative gain. The critique is right that the derivative acts on change per second. With a 10 ms step, kd x 100 x (change in signal per step) applies. At kd 0.15 a one-unit signal change gives 15 turn units, about 5250 PWM of differential, far more than the 440 I had estimated. I lower kd to 0.10. Readings are quantised and noisy (about 2%), so a 0.02 signal jitter gives about 0.2 turn units (about 70 PWM), which is tolerable. kd 0.10 still gives some damping on the slalom. If steering_oscillation is high, the first fix is kd toward 0.03 to 0.05.
- Sensor span. The outer sensors stay at x = +/-0.07 with 0.035 m spacing, so tape is still visible at a centre offset of about 0.088 m and recovery can start before the 0.06 m off-track limit. The critique notes that x = +/-0.07 lies outside the 0.06 m body half-width; I keep it deliberately, because the sensors must reach beyond the body to see the line, and the weight-2 outer sensor still gives a usable signal when it is the only one on tape.
- Sensor coverage. With 12 mm footprints and 35 mm spacing, the 25 mm tape always covers at least one sensor near centre, so there is no blind zone on the centre line.

Partly accepted:
- base_speed. I keep 1.4 (base PWM about 2866). The critique's 1.7 to 2.0 m/s figure is an assumption, since the contract gives no m/s conversion. Completion needs an average of about 1.5 m/s, so 1.4 gives little margin but avoids the penalties from line loss, which cost far more than the time term. The race's line_loss_events and completion_time will decide whether to lower it.
- kp. I keep 2.5. A full-scale signal of 2 gives 5 turn units, or 1750 PWM of differential, which the critique said was safe at base PWM 2866 (inner wheel about 1100). I have no evidence it is needed, so the race will test it.

Rejected:
- ki. The critique argues ki 0.1 overstates its value, but the contract fixes a left/right motor mismatch that a steady integral can remove. The integral is capped at +/-2 (at most 0.2 turn units), so windup risk is small. I keep ki 0.1.
- 16 mm sensors and wheel_track or wheel_radius changes. No evidence was given that these fail, and they would change the signal scale.
- Body_width. At 0.12 the off-track limit is 0.06 m, set by the floor rather than body_width, so I claim no margin from it.

Line loss: last_direction is kept. The critique's search_left/search_right alternative is not clearly better, and the lower kd reduces the derivative kick at loss.

Expected results (guesses): completion on all development tracks, 0 to 2 line-loss events, rms_error about 0.02 to 0.04 m, completion_time about 2.5 to 2.9 s. If the time is above 2.9 s with completion, speed is the limit; if line losses occur with max_error near 0.06 m, recovery is the limit; if max_error is high with few losses, kp overshoot is the limit.
